domain: school field trip lunch packing for students
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant for planning and organizing group meals. Help the user figure out what to pack for a school field trip lunch by keeping track of which students are going, their dietary needs, and any changes to the group. When the user asks you to check a list of lunch items, evaluate each item against every attending student's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm a parent volunteer helping organize packed lunches for my kid's class field trip to the science museum this Thursday. Can you help me figure out what to pack?

flow_info.value: Five kids in the lunch group: my son Ethan, plus his friends Maya, Aiden, Sofia, and Noah
Maya was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Aiden ate a PB&J at a birthday party last month and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Noah's family moved here from Ahmedabad, they're Jain
The school gave us about $8 per kid for the lunches

Sofia's mom just texted the group chat — Sofia has a fever so she's staying home Thursday. But her mom asked if we could still send a lunch box home with Ethan for Sofia since she loves the field trip lunches and would be sad to miss out
Just got back from Ethan's allergist appointment — turns out he has an egg allergy. The doctor said to avoid eggs and anything with egg as an ingredient starting immediately

The teacher just added Lily to our lunch group — she transferred into the class last week. Her mom mentioned Lily is on a strict low-sugar diet because she was just diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, they're still getting her insulin dosing stabilized

Noah's dad just called me — turns out Noah is actually staying with his uncle's family this week and they don't follow the Jain diet at all, Noah's dad said he can eat whatever the other kids are having, no restrictions

Lunch items to check: turkey and cheese pinwheel wraps (flour tortilla), hummus with carrot and celery sticks, chocolate chip granola bars, egg salad sandwich on white bread, fruit cup with grapes and strawberries, yogurt-covered pretzels

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten or wheat-based products
constraints.surface_form: Maya was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye

constraints.value: Cannot eat peanuts or peanut-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Aiden ate a PB&J at a birthday party last month and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: PB&J → peanut butter and jelly sandwich
Throat swelling + EpiPen → severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis)
Triggered by peanut butter → peanut allergy

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables
constraints.surface_form: Noah's family moved here from Ahmedabad, they're Jain
inference_chain: Jain diet → strict vegetarian, no meat, no fish, no eggs
Also avoids root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots)

constraints.value: Cannot eat eggs or foods containing egg as an ingredient
constraints.surface_form: Just got back from Ethan's allergist appointment — turns out he has an egg allergy, doctor said avoid eggs and anything with egg starting immediately

constraints.value: Must avoid high-sugar foods, needs strict low-sugar diet
constraints.surface_form: Lily is on a strict low-sugar diet because she was just diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, they're still getting her insulin dosing stabilized

constraints.value: Cannot eat eggs or egg-containing products
constraints.surface_form: Sofia's mom also mentioned in the chat that Sofia can't have eggs — she breaks out in hives

hidden_state.value: You are a parent volunteer organizing packed lunches for your son Ethan's class field trip. You will introduce 5 kids and their backgrounds across several turns. Sofia will get sick and stay home but her mom wants a lunch packed for her. Ethan gets a new allergy diagnosis. A new student Lily joins the group with diabetes. Noah's dietary restriction gets lifted. At the end you will share a list of 6 lunch items and ask if there are any issues — you must NOT hint at what specific problems to look for.

You are a calm, friendly parent volunteer. You always refer to the children and their parents by name in third person (e.g. 'Maya's mom told me...', 'Noah's dad just called...'). You never express frustration or impatience even when plans keep changing — you treat each update as normal parent-group coordination. You are matter-of-fact and pleasant.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: Hey, I'm a parent volunteer helping organize packed lunches for my kid's class field trip to the science museum this Thursday. Can you help me figure out what to pack?

aims.conversation_goal: Initiate field trip lunch planning discussion

aims.description: There are five kids in our lunch group: my son Ethan, plus his friends Maya, Aiden, Sofia, and Noah. Maya was diagnosed with celiac disease last year. Aiden ate a PB&J at a birthday party last month and his throat swelled up, they had to use an EpiPen. And Noah's family moved here from Ahmedabad, they're Jain.

aims.conversation_goal: Budget info + additional constraint for Sofia + on-topic question

aims.description: OK so I'm at the store now. I'm thinking of packing these for the group: turkey and cheese pinwheel wraps on flour tortillas, hummus with carrot and celery sticks, chocolate chip granola bars, egg salad sandwiches on white bread, a fruit cup with grapes and strawberries, and yogurt-covered pretzels. Any issues?
aims.success_criteria: Agent checks each of the 6 items against all current dietary constraints for attending kids plus Sofia's packed lunch
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 lunch items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Of the 6 items: (1) Turkey and cheese pinwheel wraps on flour tortillas — problematic for Maya because flour tortillas contain gluten and she has celiac disease. (2) Hummus with carrot and celery sticks — fine for all attending kids; Noah's Jain restriction (which would have flagged carrots as a root vegetable) has been removed. (3) Chocolate chip granola bars — problematic for Lily because they are high in sugar and she needs a strict low-sugar diet due to her type 1 diabetes; also need to check if they contain gluten (problematic for Maya). (4) Egg salad sandwiches on white bread — problematic for Ethan (egg allergy) and must also be excluded from Sofia's packed lunch (egg allergy); also problematic for Maya (white bread contains gluten). (5) Fruit cup with grapes and strawberries — fine for everyone. (6) Yogurt-covered pretzels — problematic for Maya because pretzels contain gluten; also problematic for Lily because yogurt coating is high in sugar.
required_elements: Turkey and cheese pinwheel wraps are problematic for Maya: flour tortillas contain gluten, and Maya has celiac disease
Egg salad sandwiches are problematic for Ethan: he has a newly diagnosed egg allergy
Egg salad sandwiches must be excluded from Sofia's packed lunch: Sofia has an egg allergy even though she is not attending the trip
Egg salad sandwiches are also problematic for Maya: white bread contains gluten
Chocolate chip granola bars are problematic for Lily: high sugar content conflicts with her strict low-sugar diet for type 1 diabetes
Yogurt-covered pretzels are problematic for Maya: pretzels contain gluten
Fruit cup with grapes and strawberries is fine for everyone currently in the group
Hummus with carrot and celery sticks is fine — agent does not flag carrots as a problem since Noah's Jain dietary restriction has been removed
forbidden_elements: Flagging carrots as problematic for Noah due to Jain root vegetable restriction (his restriction has been removed)
Flagging any item as problematic for Noah at all (he has no restrictions now)
Ignoring Sofia's egg allergy for her packed lunch (she is not attending but still gets a lunch box)
Saying Aiden has a general nut allergy (he specifically has a peanut allergy from the PB&J incident — none of the listed items contain peanuts)
Forgetting Lily entirely when checking items (she is a late-joining entity with a low-sugar constraint)
Treating Ethan as having no dietary restrictions (his egg allergy was added mid-conversation)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns in a school field trip lunch context. The agent must track: (1) Maya has celiac disease → cannot eat gluten/wheat (inferential), (2) Aiden had anaphylaxis from PB&J → peanut allergy specifically, NOT all nuts (inferential, over-generalization trap), (3) Noah is Jain → no meat/fish/eggs/root vegetables (inferential), but this constraint is REMOVED when his dad says he's staying with his uncle who doesn't follow the Jain diet, (4) Sofia has an egg allergy and EXITS the trip due to fever but still needs a packed lunch sent home → her egg constraint persists for her box (scope change), (5) Ethan gets a NEW egg allergy diagnosis mid-conversation (constraint addition), (6) Lily JOINS late with type 1 diabetes → strict low-sugar diet. At probe time, the current constraint state is: Maya=celiac/gluten-free, Aiden=peanut allergy, Ethan=egg allergy, Sofia=egg allergy (packed lunch only), Lily=low-sugar, Noah=no restrictions. The hummus with carrots is a trap: it looks problematic because carrots are root vegetables (Jain restriction), but Noah's restriction was removed. The fruit cup is clearly fine. The egg salad sandwich hits multiple constraints (Ethan's egg allergy, Sofia's egg allergy for her box, Maya's gluten from the bread). The granola bars and yogurt pretzels test whether the agent remembers Lily (late joiner) and Maya's gluten constraint on less obvious items.

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
